title: Social teaching, again
tomorrow: what did Mary say when the wine ran out?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Teresa with words and John in stillness: attention. Today, attention turned outward, to the back of the line.

Steam off a pot of tamales, the smell of corn and chile, a line out the door of the parish hall. Somewhere near the back is a man with no money, waiting anyway. So who gets served first? The people who paid and waited, or the one who can't pay at all? The Church has a body of teaching about exactly this kind of question, and its answer has a smell of food all over it.
screen: `STEAM, CORN, CHILE.` → `A MAN WITH NO MONEY.` → `WHO GETS SERVED FIRST?`

segments.voice: Catholic social teaching is what the Church says about justice: work, wages, families, and who gets left out. Pope Leo the Thirteenth opened a letter about workers with the Latin words Rerum Novarum, of new things, and argued that the poor, with no resources to fall back on, have a special claim to care. The Catechism names it a preferential love for those weighed down by poverty. The poor first. Not the poor only. Everyone has the same dignity. But when there's one plate and two people, the one with nothing gets it first. It comes straight from the Gospel. Jesus says in Matthew, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me." Here's the one to tell a friend: Saint Ambrose tells a story about Lawrence, a deacon in Rome. Ordered to hand over the Church's treasures, Lawrence brought out the poor, and said these were its treasures. That's the whole teaching in one scene. The poor aren't a cost the Church carries. They're its treasure. So the tamale question has an answer: feed the man at the back first. The line still gets fed. It just learns who comes first.
screen: `RERUM NOVARUM: OF NEW THINGS.` · `NOT THE POOR ONLY. THE POOR FIRST.` · `YOU DID IT TO ME.` · `LAWRENCE: THESE ARE THE TREASURES.` · then, large: `THE POOR FIRST.`

segments.voice: If there's food or a drink nearby, take one slow bite or sip and really taste it; if not, remember the last good meal you had. Then bring to mind one person who will go without today. If you pray, you can hold that person before God; if not, keep them in mind while the taste fades.
Social teaching. What the Church teaches about justice and the common good, with the poor served first.
Carry this: the poor first, because Lawrence called them the Church's treasure. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: man at Abuela's tamale sale had no money. she fed him before the whole line. fair to everyone else?
options: Fair. The Church puts the poor first, not only. The line still gets fed.
Not fair. Charity should wait until the paying customers are all served.
Only if he proves he's really poor. Otherwise people just take advantage.
chat.meaning: Catholic social teaching speaks of a preferential love for the poor: first, not only. Everyone keeps the same dignity, and everyone still eats.

Ambrose.meaning: a bishop of Milan and early Church writer

Lawrence.meaning: a deacon of Rome remembered as a martyr

deacon.meaning: an ordained minister who serves, especially the poor

Ambrose, De Officiis II.28.140: Lawrence shows the poor as the Church's treasures. Paraphrased, no quotation marks; confirm.
